title: Observer lifecycle and incident runloop for LLM serving
content:
> **Archived 2024-02-15:** this page is superseded by "Observer lifecycle and incident runloop for LLM serving" and is kept for reference only.

Overview

Purpose: describes the observer lifecycle and incident runloop for Redwood's model-serving surface (hosted API, Dedicated, Private), together with runbooks, postmortem expectations, on-call rotation guidance and status page examples. Audience: on-call engineers, SREs, support and product owners.

Scope: model-serving API endpoints, inference runtime clusters, KV/prefix caching, routing/fallback policies and anything that directly affects inference SLOs (p95 latency, error-rate, availability). Not covered: billing incidents, non-inference control plane failures and infra provider outages (see eng-sre/runbooks).

1) Roles and responsibilities

- Primary on-call (Responder): first investigator and incident owner until handoff; runs triage, mitigation and initial comms.
- Bridge operator (if invoked): runs the bridge, coordinates stakeholders, maintains a running summary.
- Escalation on-call (Area owner): team-level escalation for runtime, routing or infra fixes.
- SRE incident lead: validates mitigations and approves wider changes (autoscaler, capacity swaps).
- Customer-facing comms (Support / CS): publishes customer messages from the status templates.

2) Severity classification and SLO thresholds

Three severity tiers; assign during triage and show on the ticket and status page.

Severity | Definition | Target response | Escalation window
---------|------------|-----------------|-------------------
P1       | Large-scale outage: >25% of production requests affected OR p95 latency >5x SLO for >5 min | Acknowledge within 5 min | Escalate to SRE & product within 10 min
P2       | Partial outage: single region or class degraded, p95 latency 2–5x SLO | Acknowledge within 15 min | Escalate within 60 min if unresolved
P3       | Localized regression with mitigation available; no major customer disruption | Acknowledge within 2 hours | Triage next business day

SLOs (example):
- p95 latency: 300 ms (hosted small models)
- error-rate: <0.2% (5xx + timeouts at API edge)
- availability: 99.9% monthly

3) Incident lifecycle and runloop

1. Signal and detection
   - Alerts from Prometheus metrics, Jaeger tracing anomalies and customer reports; prioritize signals affecting p95 and error-rate.
   - Capture: top-5 alert graphs, time window, affected regions and models, recent deploys, queue depth growth.

2. Acknowledge & declare
   - Primary on-call acknowledges within the severity window.
   - For P1/P2, open an incident bridge (Zoom/Google Meet) and an incident ticket in Jira/Status.

3. Triage (first 10 min)
   - Establish blast radius: regions, customer subsets, models, routing tiers.
   - Check recent deploys (commit, rollout ID); a deploy within the last 15 minutes is the prime suspect.
   - Review autoscaling events, GPU preemptions and queue backlog.

4. Mitigate
   - Preferred: fall back to a compatible model variant, reduce QPS via routing policy, enable prefix cache, raise concurrency on affected nodes, or scale the reserve pool.
   - Confirm p95 and error-rate trend back toward SLO.

5. Stabilize & communicate
   - Once p95 is acceptable or a durable mitigation is in place, post a status update with summary, impact, next steps, ETA and owner.

6. Recovery & post-incident work
   - After 30–60 minutes of stability, close with a remediation plan and schedule the postmortem.

4) Escalation cheat-sheet

- p95 > 2x SLO for >10 min with rising error-rate: escalate to SRE incident lead.
- Queue depth > 10x baseline with rising tail latency: add reserved nodes and notify infra.
- Suspected rollout: pause immediately and roll back if safe.

5) Runbook: High-latency model-serving cluster

Immediate checklist (in order):
1. Collect evidence:
   - kubectl get pods -n runtime -l app=model-serving -o wide
   - prometheus query: rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]) and topk(10, increase(request_errors_total[5m]))
   - curl -sS "https://observability.internal/api/top-traces?service=model-serving&window=5m"
2. Check recent rollouts: deployctl history runtime/model-serving --since 30m
3. Inspect nodes: nvidia-smi; kubectl describe pod <pod> | egrep -i "OOM|Evicted|Preempt"
4. Quick mitigations:
   - Route to fallback pool: curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/route/update -d '{"policy":"fallback","target_pool":"reserve"}'
   - Raise MAX_CONCURRENCY on runtime/model-serving to 64 via deployment patch.
5. Verify with synthetic load against the affected model variant and measure p95.

Include in the ticket: p50/p95/p99 latency, API 5xx and 429 counts, queue depth and wait time, CPU/GPU utilization per node pool.

6) Postmortem & RCA

- Postmortem draft due within 5 business days of incident stabilization for P1/P2; within 14 days for P3.
- Action items carry owners and deadlines.
- PM and SRE agree on final severity and external comms.

Template: title; incident ID, severity, start/end; 2–3 sentence summary; minute-level timeline for the first 60 minutes then hourly; root cause and contributing factors; short- and long-term corrective actions (owner + due date); follow-ups (automation, tests, monitoring, runbook updates); customer impact and comms log.

7) On-call rotations and tooling

- Cadence: 1-week primary, 1-week secondary (shadow), then 2 weeks off.
- Handoff: 30-minute overlap for verbal handoff and ticket review.
- Holiday coverage: explicit backup; team lead approves changes 1 week ahead.

Handoff checklist: open incidents and priority tickets; health dashboard (tail latency, error-rate, queue backlog, GPU pool utilization, open status-page incidents); calendar and Slack contact.

Commands:
- pagerctl ack <alert-id>
- incidentctl create --service model-serving --severity P1 --summary "<short>"
- alertctl mute --rule <rule-name> --expires 15m (document reason)

8) Status page principles

- Timely, factual, concise; three updates: Acknowledged, Mitigating, Resolved.
- Include impact scope, affected models/regions, workaround, ETA if known, owner contact.

Example (Acknowledged):
  Title: Elevated inference latency impacting hosted API (US-West)
  Body: We are investigating elevated p95 latency for text generation in US-West starting 2024-01-18T11:04Z. Owner: Alex Chen. Next update: 11:20Z.

Example (Resolved):
  Title: Resolved — latency back to expected levels
  Body: Fallback routing and a rollout pause resolved the incident. A postmortem will follow within 5 business days.

9) Runbook maintenance

- Every runbook lists an owner and a quarterly review date.
- Postmortems trigger runbook updates when procedures change.
- On update: verify commands and endpoints, confirm ACLs, test mitigation scripts in staging.

Appendix
- Observability dashboard: https://observability.internal/d/model-serving
- Incident ticket template: incidentctl template --name model-serving
- On-call schedule: https://oncall.internal/teams/model-serving

Contact: #eng-oncall or a doc change request to Alex Chen.

Revision history:
- 2023-09-04: Initial draft
- 2024-01-22: Added high-latency runbook and status page examples
